classes.content: User instructions; all source column names and types; detected period or scenario values; mapping proposals and warnings; and at most the first 10 rows projected to candidate period, date, amount, units, discount, COGS, reporting-dimension and calculation-grain columns. The complete file is processed locally for inspection; unrelated columns are omitted from the built-in row preview. A separate targeted inspection may show at most 10 rows from no more than 12 explicitly named columns.
classes.purpose: Establish the comparison and candidate semantic mapping before calculation

classes.content: The complete selected population is calculated locally. The default model context contains mapped variance results, summaries, recipes, prepared-data lineage, standard and root-cause contexts, chart data and images, diagnostics, limitations and hypotheses, but not raw source rows, the original source filename or unmapped column names in the model-use manifest. Exact in-scope source matches can be produced only for a reason-recorded request using reviewed mapped filters and output columns and the exact sealed used-recipe bytes; every exact match is returned without sampling. The review widget payload contains at most the 50 largest driver rows plus artifact and follow-up metadata.
classes.purpose: Interpret the reconciled variance from reviewed mappings and complete deterministic calculations

classes.content: The first validation may receive the bounded review payload. When the stored run package matches, later render, save and apply calls use an expiring local token bound to the review_payload.json hash and run ID. Vera performs no automatic anonymization or pseudonymization.
classes.purpose: Render and record review decisions without repeatedly copying the full review package through MCP calls

classes.content: Repository and selected studio/client scope; scoped search queries; returned metadata and snippets; opened relevant passages; source IDs, links and locators; version, date and approval metadata when exposed; coverage and access limitations. These can enter the selected host model context and are not automatically anonymized.
classes.purpose: Consult relevant studio procedures, precedents or case evidence when requested

external_boundaries.content: Published shared package names and version constraints plus ordinary package-index request metadata. No client files, prompts, case data, credentials, or generated work are sent by this runtime installer.
controls: Only published shared core and explicitly selected OCR recipes are installed; package names are never derived from client material or prompts.

Host network denials stop package retrieval. Retry only the same declared setup after the host user or administrator authorizes registry access; never change host network settings or use an alternate installer to evade a denial.

Readiness probes the managed CPython 3.12 interpreter locally with isolated Python and site loading disabled, checks completed installation metadata, then checks the selected declared package versions and component imports in that interpreter. Recipe revisions, backend bytes and historical platform labels do not block a compatible environment. Compatible reuse leaves installation receipts unchanged; actual missing or incompatible dependencies require serialized repair.
All three products and their modules use the same environment. Optional OCR requires approval and is then retained in that environment. A shared environment is not a boundary between client matters.
external_boundaries.destination: Python Package Index (PyPI) or the package index configured for the active Python interpreter
external_boundaries.purpose: Prepare the published shared Vera, Clara and Lucia core requirements and explicitly approved optional OCR in one user-scoped Python 3.12 environment per operating-system host.
external_boundaries.retention: Packages remain in one fixed user-scoped environment outside plugin source and client folders until explicitly removed. The default location is ~/.local/share/mparanza/runtime/venv on macOS and Linux, and LOCALAPPDATA/mpr/venv on Windows; MPARANZA_RUNTIME_ROOT may override the parent. Enabled OCR remains enabled across later core updates. Package-index request-log retention is controlled by the configured index. Failed updates invalidate the readiness receipt and require repair before execution; this shared environment has no retained generations. Verified temporary code copies are owned by the creating command and removed after completion, failure or cooperative cancellation, with process-exit retry if deletion is temporarily blocked. Preflight verification does not lease a persistent code copy. Installed code, client files and retained professional outputs are not removed. Forced termination or power loss may leave an orphan. On macOS and Linux, fresh code snapshots and native bootstrap copies have private sidecar device/inode records and shared kernel flock leases. Detached native workers inherit the snapshot lease. Normal termination signals stop intake and retain accepted jobs until completion; SIGKILL or power loss can leave copies, recovered on a later verified startup only after an exclusive nonblocking lease proves no holder remains and the directory identity matches. Unmarked historical copies, replaced directories, symlinks and live leases are retained. Lease records contain technical directory identity only, remain outside the indexed code and client folders, and are not returned to the model or sent to a service. Windows retains process-owned cleanup without automatic POSIX orphan recovery. Managed CLI command children independently acquire and inherit the same snapshot lease before launch; a terminated launcher cannot release a surviving helper's code. The child keeps that kernel lease until its actual exit. Automatic recovery accepts only lease protocol 2, which guarantees both native-worker and CLI-child inheritance. Older protocol-1 records remain uncollected even without a holder, because legacy helpers may be untracked; current CLI calls may still borrow their leases.

external_boundaries.content: The fixed CPython 3.12 version request, operating-system and architecture selection, and ordinary download request metadata. Setup does not read client files or add prompts, case material or generated reports to this request.
controls: Use an installed CPython 3.12 when available; otherwise use uv or automatically download the published uv 0.12.10 wheel, verify its pinned SHA-256, and provision private CPython 3.12 without changing system Python or shell profiles.
Probe the selected interpreter before creating the dependency environment; never fall back to executing workflows with another Python minor version.
A failed download or interpreter probe stops setup; existing environments and client files remain intact.
external_boundaries.destination: PyPI files.pythonhosted.org for the pinned uv bootstrap, and Astral python-build-standalone CPython distributions on GitHub
external_boundaries.purpose: Provision the single supported CPython 3.12 interpreter when it is absent, automatically bootstrapping uv if needed
external_boundaries.retention: When uv must be bootstrapped, the bootstrap executable and private interpreter remain inside shared runtime storage until removed. Download request-log retention is controlled by the providers.

external_boundaries.content: Random installation UUID and opaque capability, Vera/host/runtime versions, platform and workflow technical IDs, failed stage, complete available technical diagnostic chains and measurements, explicit missing-measurement reasons, retry IDs and actual recovery outcomes. No professional helper stdout, client documents, case text, user prompts or arbitrary task logs. Known path, email and credential patterns are removed from technical messages; this mechanical filter does not establish semantic privacy. The host agent must select technical evidence without unrelated personal/client material. The remote channel does not read local files. Failed helpers retain complete stderr privately on disk; stderr may include unrelated private/client text and is read by the selected host model for semantic review under its existing account. Raw stderr is not forwarded to Mparanza. Only reviewed relevant technical diagnostics, linked by the original report UUID, are submitted as supplemental evidence. Professional stdout is not captured. Dynamic exception/argument values, locals, professional stdout and arbitrary source excerpts are not part of these structured events. The remote connector is independent of local command-process startup. If the host cannot expose/connect it, no successful report is claimed.
Only two built-in setup/preparation retries may execute automatically, once per remedy revision. Client documents, ACLs and security settings are not changed.
A published update is not recovery. The failed operation must actually execute successfully before that installation delivery closes.

Supplemental diagnostics require ownership of the original report and matching execution metadata; they are stored separately and cannot change the original report UUID, delivery status or remedy revision. Raw local diagnostic files can only be removed by acknowledging a matching recorded supplement.
Actionable remedies target an explicit original report. Each delivery uses its own applicable revision; a different report with the same generic signal does not inherit that remedy.

A cached actual connector status permits only the two fixed retries for an existing matching local receipt and latest report. It performs no direct HTTP polling or identity adoption. Missing local receipts cannot be fabricated to authorise a retry.

A helper success records readiness. Host AI verification of the original task and inputs is required for all recovered outcomes, including setup/startup. Delayed failures cannot reopen an already recovered episode.
Failed fixed retries retain complete stderr privately for semantic review. Raw recovery stderr is not automatically transmitted.

An explicitly selected MPARANZA_INCIDENT_DELIVERY=local-only setting blocks automatic client HTTP transport for this execution while preserving local evidence. Incident queues are durably marked and not automatically flushed later; this does not make model-provider processing local-only.

The service retains incident, report, remedy and outcome records; no automatic deletion period is enforced. Status access is scoped by the opaque capability. Pending diagnostic pointers and raw stderr persist in the private incident directory until a matching actual recorded supplementation receipt is acknowledged; unsuccessful review or delivery retains them. Supplementation never replaces the original recovery episode or reopens recovered records. Recorded original/outcome receipts can acknowledge only their exact local queued UUID without replacing the local capability or saved connector identity. Remedy revisions are retained from the surviving migration revision onward; overwritten legacy revisions are not reconstructed.

security_controls.control: Setup validates package-relative selections and installs the published shared recipe. No package names or dependency instructions are accepted from client documents.
security_controls.on_violation: An unknown module, missing requirements file, invalid target, or failed dependency validation stops the helper instead of executing it in a partial environment.

security_controls.control: One fixed environment is located outside plugin source and client folders. An exclusive operating-system installation lock waits for running managed Python readers, which hold a shared lease through a startup hook. Setup removes the ready receipt before mutation and restores it only after pip check and component validation. Failed setup leaves execution unavailable until repair. Symlink roots, locks and metadata are rejected. The installer is launched from base Python to avoid self-deadlock. This lease is concurrency protection, not a security sandbox. Other historical environments are not automatically deleted. State metadata normally uses atomic replacement. Only EXDEV or Windows error 17 falls back under the same installer lock to a single-link regular-file write with full-byte writes and fsync. Failed writes attempt to restore existing metadata or remove a newly created file; the ready receipt remains invalid until setup succeeds. This fallback is local and does not add a recipient or payload.
security_controls.on_violation: A target creation or validation failure returns a bounded setup error and the requested helper is not run.

security_controls.control: For the six explicitly supported assured modules, the launchers verify the complete package inventory and stable regular-file bytes against the embedded build-generated SHA-256 index. Symlinks, reparse entries, special files, extra directories/files, missing or changed code and unstable reads stop preparation. Unchanged hardlinked package code is materialized into a fresh private OS temporary directory; each copied file is re-read and must have one physical link, then the unchanged component integrity validator must pass. The managed installation and aliases are not modified. The copy contains indexed product code/assets, not client documents, credentials, workflow reports or dependency environments. This local index detects package drift; it is not a publisher signature, a signed origin attestation or proof of installed-host acceptance. The command releases its own temporary code copy after success, failure or cancellation; process-exit cleanup retries pending copies. Ownership is recorded by process ID and directory identity, so borrowed installations, caller paths and replaced roots are not deleted. Forced termination, power loss or persistent file locks can leave an orphan. Cleanup failures log the temporary path and local OS error; they do not add an external recipient or transmit client content. The root-level host .in_use directory is non-executable bookkeeping: only ASCII numeric, ordinary single-link regular marker files are excluded from the product inventory. Nested directories, links, reparse points and non-numeric names there are rejected. Marker contents are not read, executed, transmitted or included in a recovery copy; host markers and installed product files are not modified. On macOS and Linux, fresh code snapshots and native bootstrap copies have private sidecar device/inode records and shared kernel flock leases. Detached native workers inherit the snapshot lease. Normal termination signals stop intake and retain accepted jobs until completion; SIGKILL or power loss can leave copies, recovered on a later verified startup only after an exclusive nonblocking lease proves no holder remains and the directory identity matches. Unmarked historical copies, replaced directories, symlinks and live leases are retained. Lease records contain technical directory identity only, remain outside the indexed code and client folders, and are not returned to the model or sent to a service. Windows retains process-owned cleanup without automatic POSIX orphan recovery. Managed CLI command children independently acquire and inherit the same snapshot lease before launch; a terminated launcher cannot release a surviving helper's code. The child keeps that kernel lease until its actual exit. Automatic recovery accepts only lease protocol 2, which guarantees both native-worker and CLI-child inheritance. Older protocol-1 records remain uncollected even without a holder, because legacy helpers may be untracked; current CLI calls may still borrow their leases.
security_controls.on_violation: Preparation failures and host permission denials stop execution. A failed private copy is removed; no installation chmod/unlink/manual repair, alternate sandbox or relaxed component validation is permitted.

security_controls.control: The parent Vera launcher reports a negative exit code or 137/247 as forced termination. It writes execution_failure.json only inside the selected workflow context output directory or its normalization/sample subdirectories; without that matching context it logs only. The diagnostic stores workflow/run identifiers, exit status and an explicit statement that memory exhaustion is not established by the exit code. It makes no model calls or network requests.
security_controls.on_violation: A worker failure remains failure; diagnostic persistence errors are logged rather than converted into a success.

security_controls.control: The standalone Python bootstrap passes uv only declared host paths, locale, proxy, CA and cache settings, preserving original environment-name casing. Unrelated token/API-key variables and inherited UV_*, VIRTUAL_ENV, CONDA_PREFIX, PYTHONHOME and PYTHONPATH are excluded; private UV_PYTHON_* and UV_CACHE_DIR values are set by the bootstrap. The same environment is used for interpreter discovery and its local probe.
security_controls.on_violation: Undeclared environment names are absent from every bootstrap child process.

security_controls.control: The built-in incident dependency-setup retry uses the shared host/runtime environment allowlist, named runtime/state locations and recovery recursion guard instead of inheriting unrelated user tokens and keys.
security_controls.on_violation: Undeclared environment names are absent from the child environment.

security_controls.control: When the maintained launcher itself runs under Python -I -B, it restores only its own resolved scripts directory for sibling technical-diagnostic imports. It does not add the caller working directory. Helper execution, diagnostic retention and explicit incident delivery policy remain unchanged.
security_controls.on_violation: The maintained launcher must stop rather than resolving technical diagnostics from the caller working directory.

Legacy anonymous OAuth authorization remains available to old installations and for ownership migration; new plugin packages use ordinary HTTPS with local capabilities or a browser cookie. The server stores token/code hashes, technical callback metadata and a random connection UUID. No personal account signup, user profile, email or client-file permission is involved. Raw stderr is not forwarded to Mparanza. Only reviewed relevant technical diagnostics, linked by the original report UUID, are submitted as supplemental evidence. Professional stdout is not captured. Installation-preparation failures submit only a fixed technical message, exception type/errno, or the indexed package-relative file name and expected/observed SHA-256 values for a content mismatch. No altered file contents or professional files are read for this report. Managed helpers also send source-bound exception classes, OS error numbers, package-relative stack coordinates, developer-authored error templates and missing required option names automatically. Dynamic exception/argument values, locals, professional stdout and arbitrary source excerpts are not part of these structured events. Actual worker interpreter/platform fields are separate from the reporter's interpreter. Capture completeness, pending semantic review, exact remedy/retry events and host verification of the original task remain distinct evidence states; a structured event is not a semantic diagnosis. Current reporting-process version, protocol capabilities and server last-seen time are retained per process session, separately from historical failure versions; they do not establish that all conversations updated. Native-host binding, when invoked, accepts a random host UUID and scoped capability plus an optional explicit native-app label at the same incident service. Only the host capability hash is retained server-side. Stable app-profile UUIDs are derived from host UUID and app label; reporter-instance UUIDs may be task-local and do not count physical computers, plugin copies or people. App grouping grants no additional client status or outcome access. Operator views retain each original report, supplement, outcome and retry event with its actual reporting owner and server receipt time; missing historical task identity is not reconstructed. The native stdio identity bridge verifies its indexed entry, reporter, technical collector and product metadata, then executes an isolated temporary reporter snapshot using existing Python without installing dependencies. Its tool accepts only an existing reporter capability and sends host proof to the fixed register endpoint; it never returns the device key or copies the reporter key into the host identity file. Native broker version/session observations are retained separately from guest reporter and failure-worker observations. When local tools are unavailable, browser reporting depends on the host exposing permitted browser controls. If those controls are absent, delivery remains unverified. Browser identity is distinct from physical-host linkage; no device controls or folder permissions are expanded automatically. Native-helper failures return source-bound exception classes, errno or HTTP status, package-relative frames and developer-authored templates. Dynamic diagnostic values are not returned; unavailable capture is explicit. This bridge does not return raw stderr or device keys. The central recovery agent may request named technical evidence surfaces through a diagnostic-request remedy. The host AI replies with reviewed technical facts, the original report UUID and request revision. Original-task availability is represented by technical booleans, not task text, client identifiers or file contents. A resume remedy communicates a diagnosed correction to the existing authorized workflow; it does not carry executable code. Technical requests, response UUIDs, applicable revisions and their observed status are retained with the original episode. The central agent may implement and deploy incident-related software fixes through reviewed source and green CI under Fabio’s explicit recovery authorization; it does not receive professional case files or gain user-host permissions. Handled Studio Archive exceptions log their active traceback locally before returning the existing error JSON, allowing the same source-bound collector and host semantic review to retain their actual cause. The operator derives diagnostic publication, exact owner/report/revision receipt and reply states, the existing 15-minute deadline and reporting-owner last service contact from retained records. These delivery facts do not establish physical-host availability, diagnosis or original-task recovery. The operator also projects exact delivery, retry and original-task outcome evidence for all actionable remedy kinds, including software updates. Its 15-minute attention cadence is not an execution timeout. A local alert renderer uses technical incident facts and an AI-reviewed blocker, accountable next action, reason and scheduled check. An optional operator-maintained device label is accepted only with a recorded exact-device verification reference; it is not inferred from the recipient, OS or reporter identity. Rendered operator alerts may include opaque machine/case codes and a verified operator-device label, but no client contents, raw diagnostics, personal identifiers or credentials. The renderer neither sends email nor accesses the registry or client files. It rejects stale followup reviews and cannot assign an unreceived or overdue remedy back to the uncontacted Clara. Recovered labels require matching actual original-task success evidence; incomplete historical bindings remain unknown. The shared API also exposes a separate public workflow-testing endpoint: an allowlisted map of pipeline IDs to testing levels and baseline metadata, without incident details, computer IDs, run IDs or user feedback. Its reset is operator-only and does not change incident records. Native workflow transport supplies the same existing host proof during registration when it is available. The shared managed launcher also reports handled PDF recovery failures and subsequent attempts for journal-sampling and journal-bank-reconciliation. It projects fixed strategy/check identifiers, pass/fail/replay flags and attempt/readable-row counts only; PDF text, amounts, paths, adapter code and free-text rationale remain local. Supplements reuse the original report identity across process sessions and cannot certify original-task recovery. Other products carry the shared implementation but do not expose these journal workflows. Bank PDF inspection failures and subsequent corrections are linked per source, independently of journal failures. The bank source digest used in the episode key stays in local reporting state and is not added to transmitted evidence. Other bank statements cannot inherit that extraction recovery. The same native bridge also exposes the fixed task-usage operations documented by the workflow-usage service, with a verified usage-client/catalogue snapshot and task-scoped persistence. Those operations use the existing installation/computer capabilities internally and do not accept credentials, paths, commands or client documents. Error results include SQLite symbolic error codes where available; no raw database contents or diagnostic values are returned. Producer-authored exception measurements may additionally include integer and boolean technical facts with technical identifiers. The Archive state-directory rejection supplies observed POSIX mode, forbidden permission bits, private creation mode, owner/process UID and GID, directory/symlink flags, selection source (explicit, environment or default), and whether creation was requested. It does not transmit the directory path, environment values, client contents, exception arguments or locals. The operator alert displays these facts and package stack coordinates only for its exact original report and linked supplements. The replacement transport preserves the same closed reporting payloads. Browser cookies and optional original local credentials authenticate only; they are not diagnostic fields. Browser status and acknowledgements enter the selected host model context when the agent reads the rendered response. The schema view returns field definitions, not stored user data. The browser fallback sends no professional documents or raw model-data report.

Local native incident and workflow tools send ordinary HTTPS using the retained private installation owner. The plugin declares no remote MCP connection. When local execution is unavailable, the agent can operate the independently hosted recovery page using the host permitted browser controls. No browser capability or host approval is assumed. The browser authenticates with a Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, host-only cookie. POST requests require the fixed same-origin Origin and custom header; no CORS is enabled. An expired or missing previously known capability does not silently create a new owner. Schema discovery exposes the product-bound operation contract without MCP discovery.

The retained legacy MCP endpoint for old releases requires OAuth access tokens for its fixed incident resource; new plugin packages do not declare that endpoint. Authorization uses S256 PKCE, exact registered callbacks and a single-use five-minute code. Refresh tokens rotate and a replay revokes the grant; raw OAuth credentials are never placed in model prompts or stored server records.

Actual cached browser or legacy connector status reconciles only readiness hints bound to existing local report receipts. Readiness becomes action-required evidence rather than recovery; already recovered matching hints are cleared and unlinked hints are retained. No remote receipt is fabricated and no case inputs are inferred.

Before reporting an installation-preparation failure, the preflight verifies the reporting script, preflight script and product metadata against a stable build index, then snapshots them in a fresh private temporary directory and executes the reporter in isolated Python. Original-installation, cwd and PYTHONPATH imports are excluded. Damaged workflow code does not run. Unverifiable reporting components require the independent browser route when the host permits it; queued delivery never implies recorded or recovered.

A diagnostic reply requires ownership and exact original execution metadata, plus a retained diagnostic-request revision targeting that original report. A late reply cannot answer a newer request. A diagnostic exchange cannot be marked recovered.

Operator publications can require the inspected current revision. Identical applicable remedies are idempotent and do not create another retry episode. Resume instructions use existing verified workflow tools and ordinary professional gates; service text is never executed as a command.

The shared implementation binds registrations, retained legacy OAuth resources, task events, report signatures, feedback and update downloads to one product. Existing unmapped installations and receipt schema 1 remain Vera. Physical-computer identity is shared, while usage catalogues and testing epochs are separated by product.

An explicitly selected MPARANZA_INCIDENT_DELIVERY=local-only setting blocks incident HTTP transport and persists event and task restrictions, including a successful initial execution with no incident. Legacy globally suppressed entries stay local while unrelated automatic tasks can report. Native retries and supplements honor retained permissions. Authorizing one retained report checks its installation, task, report UUID and canonical content hash locally without sending; only those exact bytes can subsequently be sent. Corrections do not inherit authorization for changed bytes. Authorization metadata stays local and adds no external payload field. This does not make model-provider processing local-only.

PDF recovery evidence uses the existing durable outbox and exact original-report supplementation, including local-only delivery. Readable partial results and independent workflow gates survive incident-service failure. Frozen extraction is explicitly unqualified and never generates a recovered outcome.

When a native execution supplies its retained task UUID, newly created local incident entries and operation identities carry that scope. Failure/progress delivery and success recovery select only that task. Older queued evidence and receipts are neither relabelled, removed nor transmitted by the task. The scope stays local and adds no external report field; unscoped maintenance remains a separate operation.

The technical_facts transport accepts at most 100 integer or boolean values and bounded technical identifier keys. Automatic collection reads only the producer-declared exception field; it does not inspect locals or serialize arbitrary string values. The existing host review path remains available for relevant technical context that cannot be captured by these measurements.

An expired or missing previously known capability does not silently create a new owner. Schema discovery exposes the product-bound operation contract without MCP discovery.

Original local credentials can link or restore their owner over HTTPS. A legacy OAuth owner can request a five-minute, single-use transfer code while the old connection is still available. Only hashes of browser tokens and transfer codes are stored. Transfer preserves original record owners and links already authenticated browser history. The code is submitted in the request body, never a URL. Lost or revoked credentials do not prove ownership and cannot be replaced by a new identity to claim old history.

Successful native status stores the exact pending-remedy snapshot locally for automatic managed retry progress, including an empty snapshot. A failed status retains the last known snapshot. Reading status does not execute remedies; original operation, input, report and revision checks still govern closure. No new external report fields or recipients are introduced.

data_sent.content: Random installation UUID and opaque capability, Clara/host/runtime versions, platform and workflow technical IDs, failed stage, complete available technical diagnostic chains and measurements, explicit missing-measurement reasons, retry IDs and actual recovery outcomes. Known path, email and credential patterns are removed from technical messages; this mechanical filter does not establish semantic privacy. The host agent must select technical evidence without unrelated personal/client material. The remote channel does not read local files. Legacy anonymous OAuth authorization remains available to old installations and for ownership migration; new plugin packages use ordinary HTTPS with local capabilities or a browser cookie. The server stores token/code hashes, technical callback metadata and a random connection UUID. No personal account signup, user profile, email or client-file permission is involved. Failed helpers retain complete stderr privately on disk; stderr may include unrelated private/client text and is read by the selected host model for semantic review under its existing account. Raw stderr is not forwarded to Mparanza. Only reviewed relevant technical diagnostics, linked by the original report UUID, are submitted as supplemental evidence. Professional stdout is not captured. Installation-preparation failures submit only a fixed technical message, exception type/errno, or the indexed package-relative file name and expected/observed SHA-256 values for a content mismatch. No altered file contents or professional files are read for this report. Managed helpers also send source-bound exception classes, OS error numbers, package-relative stack coordinates, developer-authored error templates and missing required option names automatically. Process-session UUIDs, persistent operation UUIDs and optional keyed digests of existing run/input-receipt identities bind attempts without disclosing receipt fields or raw client-input hashes. Actual worker interpreter/platform fields are separate from the reporter's interpreter. Capture completeness, pending semantic review, exact remedy/retry events and host verification of the original task remain distinct evidence states; a structured event is not a semantic diagnosis. Current reporting-process version, protocol capabilities and server last-seen time are retained per process session, separately from historical failure versions; they do not establish that all conversations updated. Native-host binding, when invoked, accepts a random host UUID and scoped capability plus an optional explicit native-app label at the same incident service. Only the host capability hash is retained server-side. Stable app-profile UUIDs are derived from host UUID and app label; reporter-instance UUIDs may be task-local and do not count physical computers, plugin copies or people. App grouping grants no additional client status or outcome access. Operator views retain each original report, supplement, outcome and retry event with its actual reporting owner and server receipt time; missing historical task identity is not reconstructed. The native stdio identity bridge verifies its indexed entry, reporter, technical collector and product metadata, then executes an isolated temporary reporter snapshot using existing Python without installing dependencies. Its tool accepts only an existing reporter capability and sends host proof to the fixed register endpoint; it never returns the device key or copies the reporter key into the host identity file. Native broker version/session observations are retained separately from guest reporter and failure-worker observations. When local tools are unavailable, browser reporting depends on the host exposing permitted browser controls. If those controls are absent, delivery remains unverified. Browser identity is distinct from physical-host linkage; no device controls or folder permissions are expanded automatically. Native-helper failures return source-bound exception classes, errno or HTTP status, package-relative frames and developer-authored templates. Dynamic diagnostic values are not returned; unavailable capture is explicit. This bridge does not return raw stderr or device keys. The host AI replies with reviewed technical facts, the original report UUID and request revision. Original-task availability is represented by technical booleans, not task text, client identifiers or file contents. Technical requests, response UUIDs, applicable revisions and their observed status are retained with the original episode. These delivery facts do not establish physical-host availability, diagnosis or original-task recovery. The operator also projects exact delivery, retry and original-task outcome evidence for all actionable remedy kinds, including software updates. Its 15-minute attention cadence is not an execution timeout. A local alert renderer uses technical incident facts and an AI-reviewed blocker, accountable next action, reason and scheduled check. An optional operator-maintained device label is accepted only with a recorded exact-device verification reference; it is not inferred from the recipient, OS or reporter identity. Rendered operator alerts may include opaque machine/case codes and a verified operator-device label, but no client contents, raw diagnostics, personal identifiers or credentials. The renderer neither sends email nor accesses the registry or client files. It rejects stale followup reviews and cannot assign an unreceived or overdue remedy back to the uncontacted Clara. Recovered labels require matching actual original-task success evidence; incomplete historical bindings remain unknown. The shared API also exposes a separate public workflow-testing endpoint: an allowlisted map of pipeline IDs to testing levels and baseline metadata, without incident details, computer IDs, run IDs or user feedback.
